verses.text: So what do Jewish people have going for them? What’s the point of circumcision?
Actually, a lot. First, God trusted the Jewish people with his messages.
What if some didn’t stay faithful? Does their unfaithfulness cancel out God’s faithfulness?
Not a chance! God stays true, even if every human turns out to be a liar. Scripture says, “So you’ll be proved right by what you say and win when you’re judged.”
But if our wrong choices make God’s goodness stand out, what are we supposed to say? Is God wrong to judge us? I’m talking like people do.
Absolutely not! If that were true, how could God judge the world?
If my lie makes God’s truth shine brighter and brings him glory, why am I still getting judged like a sinner?
Why not say, as some people falsely accuse us of saying, “Let’s do evil so good can come from it”? They deserve the judgment they’re getting.
So are we Jews any better? No, not at all. We’ve already shown that Jews and Greeks are all caught up under sin.
Scripture says, “Nobody is righteous—not even one.
“Nobody understands; nobody is looking for God.
“Everyone has wandered off. Together they’ve become useless. Nobody does good—not even one.”
“Their throats are open graves; their tongues tell lies.” “Viper poison sits under their lips.”
“Their mouths are full of curses and bitter words.”
“They rush to spill blood;
“destruction and misery follow their path;
“and they haven’t learned the way of peace.”
“They have zero fear of God.”
We know the Law speaks to the people under it, so every mouth gets shut and the whole world stands accountable to God.
Nobody gets made right with God by doing the Law’s checklist. The Law shows us what sin is—that’s its job.
But now God has revealed a way to make people right apart from the Law, even though the Law and Prophets pointed to it all along.
God makes right everyone who believes through faith in Jesus Christ. There’s no VIP line here;
everybody has sinned and missed God’s glory.
Still, God makes people right as a free gift, by his grace, through the rescue in Christ Jesus.
God presented Jesus as the sacrifice that deals with sin, received through faith in his blood. This showed God’s righteousness: in his patience, he had passed over sins committed earlier.
He did this to show his righteousness now, so he is both just and the one who makes right those who trust Jesus.
So where’s the flex? Gone. Did the law of works shut it down? Nope—the law of faith did.
So here’s the conclusion: people are made right by faith, apart from doing the works of the Law.
Is God only the God of Jews? Isn’t he also God of Gentiles? Of course he is.
There’s one God. He makes the circumcised right by faith and the uncircumcised right through faith.
So does faith cancel the Law? Absolutely not! We stand by the Law.
